newsitem.title: UK: Salomon reiterates "buy" on Russia's Chernogorneft.
newsitem.headline: Salomon reiterates "buy" on Russia's Chernogorneft.

text.p: Salomon Brothers has reiterated its "buy" recommendation on Russian oil company Chernogorneft CHRHY.OBB CHGZ.RTS and upgraded its valuation per share to $18.00 from $11.00.

"We have upgraded our base-case valuation to over $18.00 per share, with tax, price cost and other parameters. The shares offer even greater upside in the event of an industry recovery, with higher domestic oil prices and a reduced tax burden," Salomon analysts Igor Falaleyev and Jeremy Hudson said.
The stock was trading at $11.80 by the close on Thursday.
Salomon notes that Chernogorneft is paing too high a level of tax and is lobbying for a cut in excise tax from $15.00 per tonne of oil to $10.91.
Foreign investors own 17.96 percent of the free float of Chernogorneft shares.

Salomon is forecasting net income for the company of $33.3 million according to U.S. GAAP standards for the whole of 1996, compared with $125.5 million in 1995, and is looking for $36.9 million in 1997.

In common with other Russian oil companies, Chernogorneft is experiencing problems with collecting moneys owed to it, over the first six months of the current year, receivables grew 258 to 751 billion roubles ($147 million).

"The first galf operational and financial results indicate the approach of stabilisation and the onset of longer-term production and earnings growth," Salomon said. -- David Chance London newsroom 44 171 542 5887
